territorial_scope.description: Applies within Connecticut, limited to highways of up to four municipalities selected for the pilot program.

evidence.quote: shall establish a pilot program for not more than four municipalities

summary.short: Connecticut 2017 act creating a pilot program in which autonomous vehicle testers may test fully autonomous vehicles on highways of up to four municipalities under registration, insurance and operating conditions, plus a task force to study their regulation. Effective from passage.
summary.long: Section 1 defines fully autonomous vehicles (SAE J3016 levels four or five), operators, testers, fleet service providers and manufacturers. The Office of Policy and Management must establish a pilot program for up to four municipalities, selected by the Secretary using 2010 census population ranges, in which autonomous vehicle testers may test fully autonomous vehicles on highways. Each municipality signs a written agreement fixing locations, routes, vehicles and hours. Testing requires an operator seated at the wheel, able to take manual control and holding an operator's license; registration of each vehicle with the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles; liability insurance, self-insurance or a surety bond of at least five million dollars; and compliance with traffic law and NHTSA standards. Testing on limited access highways is prohibited. The Secretary may immediately prohibit an operator or tester posing a risk to public safety or not complying, and testers must provide performance information, withholding commercially valuable or proprietary data. The Secretary reports to the transportation committee by January 1, 2019 and annually thereafter. Section 2 creates a 14-member task force to study state regulation of fully autonomous vehicles, with interim reports due January 1 and July 1, 2018 and a final report by January 1, 2019; it terminates on the final report or January 1, 2019, whichever is later. Sections 1 and 2 take effect from passage; the act was approved June 27, 2017.

notes: Text is the act as approved June 27, 2017; no bill number or consolidated version appears in the document. Sec. 1(b) allows a pilot in up to four municipalities but states selection criteria for only two ('at least one' municipality in each population band, 2010 census). Sec. 2(g) sets interim reports for January 1, 2018 and July 1, 2018 and a final report for January 1, 2019, and provides that the task force terminates on the later of the final report date or January 1, 2019. No penalty provisions appear; the secretary's power to prohibit testing is in Sec. 1(f). The general statutes sections cited (14-1, 14-12, 11-4a) are not in the registry and are not annotated here. Only relations, entities and notes were requested; other sections are not filled.

obligations.summary: The Office of Policy and Management, in consultation with listed departments, shall establish a pilot program for up to four municipalities allowing autonomous vehicle testers to test fully autonomous vehicles on their highways.

obligations.summary: Municipalities must apply to the Secretary in the manner and form the Secretary directs for inclusion in the pilot program; the Secretary must select at least one municipality of a stated population band and one of a second stated population band.

obligations.summary: The chief elected official or chief executive officer of a selected municipality shall enter into a written agreement with a tester that at minimum specifies routes and locations, prohibits operation outside them except in emergencies, identifies each vehicle by VIN, make, year and model, and specifies operating hours.
